site.name: cloudflare-radar
site.summary: cloudflare-radar-clone Clone of the Cloudflare Radar global internet insights dashboard (single-page app). Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Single-page dashboard: top Cloudflare nav + global time / region filters; main area is a grid of cards — global traffic trends, top browsers, device types, protocol distribution, attack trends, Outage Center, Top domains, Top ASNs, etc.; each card has a chart + tooltip + "View more" entry | | `styles.css` | Card grid, chart palette, tooltip, filter bar, dark header | | `script.js` | Chart rendering (SVG / canvas), filter coordination, time-range switching, tab switching, tooltips |

run_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore the single-page Cloudflare Radar dashboard, validating the main insight-consumption flow (global filters → cards/charts → drill-in controls) plus adjacent in-page navigation, search/filter, dialogs, and responsive behavior.
run_plan.summary: This run should focus on the SPA nature of the site: most visible navigation appears to be anchor- or section-based within index.html, so coverage should emphasize section transitions, filter coordination, and card-level interactions rather than expecting separate HTML pages. Start by establishing the baseline dashboard state and verifying that top-level controls update or reposition the same page consistently, then work through major content sections and their visible actions such as tabs, time-range switches, tooltips, share/export, and 'View more' style entries. Finish with mobile validation of the highest-value flows because the prescan already shows multiple undersized tap targets in the top navigation and utility controls.
assumptions: Only index.html is a known HTML page; additional experiences, if any, are likely in-page sections, dialogs, or JS-driven states rather than separate documents.
Top nav items like Overview, Traffic, Security, Connectivity, Routing, DNS, and Reports likely jump to or activate sections within the same SPA.
Controls such as Share, Export, Add filter, Search Radar, date range, tabs, and chart affordances are expected to trigger dialogs, menus, overlays, or chart state changes on index.html.
Because script.js coordinates chart rendering, time-range switching, tab switching, and tooltips, dynamic state validation is a priority even without multiple pages.
risk_hotspots: index.html top navigation bar: many small tap targets flagged for mobile, especially Radar home, Overview/Traffic/Security/etc., API, EN, and theme toggle
index.html global filter row: LOCATION, LOOKUP search, DATE RANGE, Add filter, and Reset may have interdependent state and reset behavior
index.html Search Radar controls: both top-bar Search Radar and in-content LOOKUP field could create overlapping search UX or inconsistent results
index.html card actions: Share, Export, Copy link, Learn more, Inspect, View all, View in Data Explorer, Open query may open dialogs or alter state without clear recovery
index.html charts and tabs: HTTP requests/Bytes/Latency/Anomalies and Hourly/Daily/Weekly likely drive chart rerenders and are worth checking for visual/state consistency
index.html rankings and category tabs: All/AI/Social/Video may change list content and selected-domain detail state
index.html dialogs/overlays: prescan detected 6 dialogs, so modal layering, dismissal, and focus recovery are high-risk
index.html left-side filter navigation: section filter/search plus long category list may become difficult on mobile and may desync from main content scroll position

phases.title: Baseline and primary dashboard orientation
phases.objective: Confirm the default landing state and map how the main dashboard is organized before deep interaction.
key_checks: Verify initial default state for Worldwide location, Last 24 hours date range, and visible comparison chips/status text
Use top navigation items (Overview, Traffic, Security, Connectivity, Routing, DNS, Reports) to confirm whether they scroll, switch sections, or otherwise update active state on the same page

Use left-side section links such as Global Internet trends, HTTP requests, Traffic by type, Domain rankings, Internet outages, HTTP DDoS attacks, and Outages to verify anchor accuracy and active highlighting
Check that hero KPIs and first visible cards are readable, aligned, and consistent with the selected filters
Record whether any nav action changes URL hash, selected state, or focus/scroll position
exit_criteria: Primary sections of the dashboard are identified and reachable from both top nav and left nav
Default dashboard state is documented with no unexplained broken navigation or missing content
The run has evidence about whether navigation is anchor-based, tab-based, or mixed

phases.title: Global controls and state coordination
phases.objective: Validate the shared controls that likely drive the whole dashboard and test recovery/reset behavior.
key_checks: Interact with Worldwide location control and verify menu contents, selection feedback, and whether visible cards update coherently
Interact with DATE RANGE and switch to at least one alternate range if available; verify KPI values/charts refresh without layout breakage
Use Add filter to inspect available filter affordances and confirm whether applied filters appear as removable chips or visible state
Use Reset after making changes and verify all global controls return to the original default state
Exercise the in-content LOOKUP search field with a realistic query and verify suggestion, result, or no-result behavior if present
Compare behavior of the top Search Radar control against the in-content LOOKUP field to identify duplicated or conflicting search patterns
Check share/export utility controls from the main dashboard header for dialog opening, dismissal, and preservation of current filter state
exit_criteria: At least one non-default global state has been applied and then reset successfully
Search and filter controls have been exercised enough to understand whether they are coordinated or independent
Any dialogs/menus triggered by header controls can be closed cleanly with state recovery

phases.title: Chart cards, tabs, and drill-in actions
phases.objective: Test the highest-value analytic interactions inside cards and confirm chart state changes are understandable and stable.
key_checks: On Internet traffic, switch among HTTP requests, Bytes, Latency, and Anomalies tabs and verify chart, labels, and selected styling update correctly
Switch chart granularity controls such as Hourly, Daily, and Weekly and verify rerender quality, axis legibility, and preserved context
Hover or tap chart areas to surface tooltips where available and check content clarity, positioning, and dismissal
Use visible actions like Open query, Copy link, Learn more, Share, and overflow menu if present to verify affordance clarity and recovery
On Traffic by type, validate category percentages and any Inspect/drill-in behavior
On Protocol usage and Attacks and mitigations, test visible drill-in entries such as Explore or View in Data Explorer and note whether they open dialogs, scroll targets, or panels
Check KPI mini-cards with Details links to confirm whether they expose deeper context or simply duplicate nearby content
exit_criteria: The main chart card has been exercised across its major tabs and time granularities
At least several card-level drill-in controls have been tested with successful dismissal or return path
Tooltip and chart interactions have been observed on both desktop-style pointer interaction and at least one non-hover fallback assumption for mobile planning

phases.title: Section-specific adjacent flows
phases.objective: Cover the lower-priority but still visible adjacent dashboard sections such as rankings, resolver, outages, BGP/ASN, Data Explorer, reports, and search.
key_checks: In Domain popularity, switch category tabs like All, AI, Social, and Video and verify list ordering, movement indicators, and selected-domain detail behavior
Check any View all or Details affordances in rankings-style modules for clarity of navigation and return
Visit 1.1.1.1 resolver, Quality and outages, BGP and AS Rank, Data Explorer, Latest reports and analysis, and Search Radar sections via left nav or in-page links
Validate whether these sections are fully rendered, placeholder-like, or interactive, and test at least one visible action in each if available
Inspect long-page scrolling behavior, sticky elements, and whether the left-side navigation remains synchronized with the currently viewed section
If dialogs are present in these lower sections, confirm escape/close behavior and focus return
exit_criteria: All major visible headings/sections from the prescan have been visited at least once
At least one interaction has been attempted in each adjacent section that exposes visible controls
No major section remains unclassified as interactive, informational, or incomplete

phases.title: Mobile and responsive validation
phases.objective: Repeat the most important flows on mobile and specifically investigate known tap-target and navigation risks.
key_checks: Open the page in mobile viewport and assess whether top navigation collapses, wraps, overflows, or remains directly tappable
Retest small-tap-target items called out in prescan: Radar home, Overview/Traffic/Security/Connectivity/Routing/DNS/Reports, API, EN, and theme toggle
Verify access to search, global filters, and left-side navigation equivalents on mobile, including whether filters become drawers, accordions, or overflow panels
Repeat one end-to-end primary flow on mobile: navigate to a section, change a global filter/date range, interact with a chart tab, and recover/reset
Check chart readability and horizontal overflow on cards like Internet traffic and Traffic by type
Test dialog/menu behavior on mobile for Share, Export, Add filter, and any search overlay, including dismissal and viewport fit
exit_criteria: Critical desktop interactions have been replayed on mobile with evidence about usability differences
Known tap-target issues have been confirmed, mitigated by responsive design, or documented as genuine problems
Mobile navigation and filter access paths are understood well enough to critique the responsive UX

coverage_targets.pages: Visit the only known HTML page, index.html, and traverse all major in-page sections reachable from top nav, left nav, and card drill-ins.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise most visible controls on the dashboard: global location/date/search/filter/reset, top utility controls, section navigation, chart tabs and time switches, tooltips, rankings category tabs, and representative card actions.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat the critical dashboard flow and the highest-risk controls in a mobile viewport, with special attention to top-nav tap targets, filter access, chart readability, and dialog handling.

notes: Do not assume external pages exist unless an interaction clearly navigates away from index.html or opens a distinct route/dialog.
Given max_steps 80 and exhaustive depth, prioritize breadth across all visible sections first, then spend remaining steps on stateful controls and mobile regression of the most important flows.
Because no console or network errors were seen in prescan, the run should emphasize UX consistency, discoverability, and interaction clarity rather than load-failure hunting.

ux_notes: The click on the 'Include public DNS resolver data' checkbox did not close the Refine Radar data drawer; the drawer remains open in the screenshot with its close '×', checkboxes, and orange 'Apply filters' button still visible.

This action did not satisfy the objective of testing a clear close affordance or return to dashboard context, because the interaction only toggled a filter control and tool feedback reported no obvious visible-text or URL change.

The drawer appears to rely on an upper-right '×' for dismissal rather than providing an obvious cancel/close control near the filter actions, while the dashboard remains partially visible but occluded behind the open side panel.

step.objective: Learn whether the Refine Radar data drawer can be closed cleanly and whether users regain unobstructed context without accidental state changes.
step.success_criteria: The drawer closes via its × control, the main dashboard becomes fully visible again, and no unintended filter chips or metric changes appear.

result.feedback: No obvious URL or visible-text change was detected after the action.

Because the click failed and the page URL/visible content stayed on the same dashboard state, there is no evidence here about AI-tab active-state feedback or whether the ranked list/detail changes.

The failed interaction itself suggests a usability risk for off-screen filter controls in this dense dashboard, since an enabled visible DOM element could not be interacted with due to viewport positioning.

ux_notes: Clicking the top-nav 'Routing' link did switch the SPA into routing-focused content: the page now shows a 'Routing' heading with routing-specific copy ('Inspect BGP announcements, withdrawals, AS ranking, route leaks, and RPKI status.') and modules like 'BGP update activity' and 'BGP and AS Rank'.

Orientation cues appear synchronized after the switch: the top navigation shows 'Routing' as the active tab, and the left rail now includes a 'ROUTING' section alongside the routing-focused main content.
The URL remained 'index.html#' rather than changing to '#routing' even though the clicked link href is '#routing', so deep-link/share-state feedback is weaker despite the visible content update.

step.objective: Learn how the dashboard reflows on mobile and whether the dense top navigation and controls become accessible or break responsiveness.
step.success_criteria: A mobile screenshot/state becomes available, showing whether nav, filters, and cards collapse, overflow, or remain tappable in a usable way.

result.feedback: Captured responsive screenshots.

ux_notes: Responsive screenshots were captured, satisfying the step goal of obtaining a mobile state for comparison.

The available evidence still shows dense top-nav items with multiple mobile tap targets under the 44px guidance (e.g. Overview 83x35, Traffic 65x35, DNS 50x35, Reports 73x35), indicating navigation may remain hard to tap on smaller screens.
No console or network errors were observed during the responsive capture, so there is no evidence of runtime breakage from this action alone.

result.feedback: Visible content changed after the action.

Mobile header controls are somewhat tight for dismissal/recovery flows: the API trigger itself is only 48x38px, below 44px guidance per layout warnings.
